profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility mapped separately at 350 East Cermak Road, Chicago, IL 60616, the same street address as Digital Realty's ORD10 (Lakeside Technology Center). This session's fetch treated this as part of the same large complex rather than a separately coded property, so it is not assigned an independent square footage figure distinct from ORD10's confirmed 1,005,500 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This mapped point sits within Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint, which also includes 600 South Federal Street downtown and a cluster of suburban buildings in Elk Grove Village and Franklin Park near O'Hare International Airport. Digital Realty markets its Chicago properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage. Illinois has offered data center-specific state tax incentives, administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, that local officials have credited with helping draw large colocation and hyperscale investment to the Chicago metro.

reading.body:
Digital Realty operates Lakeside Technology Center at 350 East Cermak Road in Chicago as part of a three-location metro footprint that includes downtown and suburban properties near O'Hare. The company does not publish a separate megawatt IT capacity figure for this building on its property page or in its FY2025 Form 10-K, which discloses regional square footage and facility counts rather than per-building power ratings. The facility is mapped at roughly 1.1 million technical square feet and opened in 1999.

Illinois ranks seventh by published megawatt capacity among the 44 mapped data center facilities in the state, with six facilities statewide disclosing power figures totaling 236 MW. Lakeside Technology Center's published capacity is not among those six disclosed figures. ComEd supplies power to the Chicago metro, where state tax incentives for data centers have been credited by local officials with drawing colocation and hyperscale operators to the region.

As a colocation landlord rather than a compute operator, Digital Realty leases space to tenants that may include hyperscalers, cloud providers, or enterprise customers. The Lakeside campus sits in one of the company's four largest US metro markets alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, and Silicon Valley. Without a published power figure for this specific building, its share of Illinois and national AI infrastructure capacity cannot be read from operator disclosures alone.
